VOScript: The witch trials were not medieval. The worst of them ran through the 1500s and 1600s, at the same time as the printing press and the beginnings of modern science. Progress and panic were not separate eras. They ran side by side, in the same rooms, funded by the same people. They usually do.
BRollNeeded: printing press or old book pages turning; a candle; hands closing a heavy book
ShotNote: To camera, seated, low lamp. Say the last 3 words flat and stop. Do not soften it.

VOScript: In 1938 Orson Welles read War of the Worlds on the radio and America supposedly lost its mind. It did not. The audience that night was small. Newspapers were losing advertising to radio and they had every reason to make radio look dangerous, so they wrote the panic. The panic was a story about a story.
BRollNeeded: a radio; newspaper pages; a dial being turned; your hands
ShotNote: To camera. This is the build in public lane, so it can be the version of you that is figuring it out out loud.
SourceLine: Pooley and Socolow, research on the 1938 broadcast, 2013

VOScript: Mary Shelley was 18 when she started Frankenstein. It was 1816, the year without a summer, when ash from a volcano on the other side of the world kept Europe under cloud. She was stuck indoors in bad weather with nothing going right, and she invented a genre. The conditions were never the requirement.
BRollNeeded: rain on a window; a notebook; a candle; you writing
ShotNote: To camera, warmer light than the other 4. The last line is the whole post. Land it and hold before you cut.

VOScript: There is no confirmed case of a child being killed by a stranger's poisoned Halloween candy. Not 1. A sociologist named Joel Best has been tracking every report since 1958 and none of them hold up. A fear that changed how an entire country parents has nothing behind it at all.
BRollNeeded: a bowl of wrapped candy; a porch light; a door
ShotNote: To camera. Say it plainly, no wink. People are genuinely going to argue with you, so leave the source on screen.

VOScript: Nobody was burned at Salem. 20 people were executed in 1692. 19 were hanged, and 1, Giles Corey, was pressed to death under stones. The burning is the detail everyone repeats and it is the one detail that is wrong. Worth asking what else you are repeating.
BRollNeeded: stones; a rope; a plain wooden chair; low window light
ShotNote: To camera. Coldest of the 5. No music under the last line if you can help it.
